ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Under the Financial Transactions Reporting Act and KoFIU regulations, every formation agent and financial institution must screen each shareholder, director, and UBO against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean Government designated sanctions list issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, together with the FATF blacklist decisions. Mandatory PEP screening must be performed on a risk-weighted basis, identifying politicians, senior government officials, military officers, state enterprise leaders and their family members and close associates. All negative news, media scrutiny, bankruptcy filings, and ML/FT red flags must be documented, escalated to compliance, and subjected to enhanced due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Korean Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (Internetdeunggi-so) and the Court Registry (Beobwon) name clearance search portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal corporate name must be registered in Hangul Korean script. Any foreign or English word used in the trade name must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul following the Revised Romanization of Korean by the National Institute of Korean Language. The name must include the termination Yuhan Hoesa for an LLC and must be visually or phonetically distinguishable from all pre-existing names in the same court registry. An English-language trade name may be recorded as an auxiliary trade name in the same registration and must be separately trademark searched.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Korean court registry rejects a proposed company name for lack of distinctiveness or use of restricted tokens, the applicant may first submit a written pleading to the same registry within 14 days explaining the distinguishing element. If the registry maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Seoul Administrative Court within 90 days under the Administrative Appeals Act, or invoke the Administrative Appeal Commission of the provincial government, depending on the registered office's location. Simultaneously, the applicant may modify the name, obtain prior ministerial approval for sensitive words, or request a preparatory hearing. All appeal submissions must be in Korean and accompanied by a translated copy of the registry's written refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a freeze-dried pet raw meat manufacturing facility under ISIC 1080, the Livestock Products Sanitation Control Act and the Food Sanitation Act require a physical plant with production lines, supply storage, temperature control, and quality control reagents, preventing a virtual office or commercial mailbox from being used as the registered head office. The tax office, during business registration (saeopja deungnok), will reject a virtual address and require proof of leased or owned industrial premises. Commercial banks in Korea similarly require a physical site visit for a corporate account opening for pet food manufacturers. A virtual office may only be used for ancillary representative offices; the manufacturing entity must have a substantive physical head office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) first-time manufacturing license requires a mandatory site inspection by the local health office; (ii) annual hygiene inspection is statutorily required; (iii) unannounced spot checks may be triggered by tax anomalies, consumer complaints, or imported ingredient inbound, with 20% likelihood in the first quarter and 60% probability after an audit flag; (iv) municipal tax inspectors verify actual place of business before issuing a certificate. Quantified risk: 85% probability of at least one physical on-site inspection within the first 12 months of operation. Penalties for non-existent premises include cancellation of the business license and administrative fines up to KRW 10 million.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, administered through the HomeTax electronic portal (hometax.go.kr); export customs clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service through UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) owned partly or wholly by a foreign non-resident, registration begins after the company obtains its legal corporate existence under the Korean Commercial Act. The company must file a business registration application with the district tax office having jurisdiction over its registered domestic place of business, or through the HomeTax portal, within 20 days of commencing business. The supporting dossier must include: the articles of incorporation, a foreign company registration certificate or notarized equivalent proving the foreign shareholders, the lease or ownership certificate for the Korean business address, a domestic bank account statement, identification and residency certificates for each representative director or resident agent, and a written power of attorney appointing a tax representative if no domestic place of business can be established. NTS then issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as the company's TIN and VAT registration number. The company must thereafter register its corporate income tax obligations and VAT obligations; foreign non-resident shareholders receiving dividends or retained remuneration are separately covered by a Korean withholding registration through the same NTS tax number. A foreign corporation without a Korean place of business that is nonetheless carrying on a VAT taxable business in Korea must obtain a foreigner's business registration number through a Korean tax representative and the same HomeTax channel.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic Korean corporation subject to entity-level corporate income tax under the Corporate Income Tax Act; it is not eligible for pass-through treatment. Its worldwide income is within Korean taxing jurisdiction, and it is a VAT taxpayer under the Value-Added Tax Act once it engages in taxable supplies. No separate sub-national entity classification distinction applies in a unitary Korean jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box election or an elective hybrid entity classification regime. The company's status as a Korean domestic corporation is fixed by the Korean Commercial Act; no tax election can recharacterize the vehicle as a flow-through or transparent entity for Korean corporate tax and VAT purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Korean Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea, with a statutorily earmarked Local Consumption Tax component, administered by the National Tax Service through HomeTax.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no monetary turnover threshold for the obligation to obtain a business registration number; every person supplying taxable goods or services must register with the NTS through HomeTax within 20 days of commencing business. An individual sole proprietor whose annual taxable turnover does not exceed KRW 80,000,000 may elect simplified taxable person status, but the simplified status does not remove the business registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a mandatory electronic tax invoice (e-tax invoice) system under the Value-Added Tax Act for all general VAT taxpayers. The electronic tax invoice must be transmitted to the NTS through the HomeTax electronic tax invoice system by the end of the next day after the invoice is issued, using the approved HomeTax API or an NTS-certified ERP adapter. Korea does not operate a government pre-clearance or digital stamp clearance model comparable to Latin American fiscal control; instead, the NTS uses real-time post-issuance validation, automated matching against VAT returns and corporate income tax filings, and anti-fraud analytics to detect missing invoices. Mandatory cash receipts and credit or debit card payment data reporting provide additional transaction-level visibility.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, supplies of goods exported from the Republic of Korea to a foreign country are zero-rated at 0% VAT. For freeze-dried pet food and pet raw meat products falling under ISIC 1080, the company must prove that title to the goods passed to a foreign buyer, the goods were physically delivered outside Korea, and a Korea Customs Service export declaration was completed. The export must be evidenced by the KCS UNI-PASS export declaration and a corresponding overseas transport document. Qualifying services that are directly connected with exported goods and paid in foreign currency may also qualify, but the core manufacturing business must rely on goods export evidence. The zero-rated sale must be reported as zero-rated output VAT in the VAT return and on the electronic tax invoice, with the export declaration reference number entered in the HomeTax e-invoice record.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: UNI-PASS Electronic Export Declaration and Export Customs Clearance Confirmation (Export Declaration Number) issued by the Korea Customs Service
Original negotiable Bill of Lading or Air Waybill showing the Korean supplier as consignor and a foreign consignee or delivery address
Commercial invoice, packing list, and certificate of Korean origin or veterinary or export health certificate for animal-origin pet food

Foreign exchange bank Export Proceeds Receipt Confirmation, also known as the foreign currency purchase confirmation, issued by a Korean Foreign Exchange Bank for the collection of the export sales consideration
Zero-rated VAT electronic tax invoice transmitted to the NTS HomeTax system showing the export declaration reference
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: NTS and Korea Customs Service audits may reassess a claimed export zero-rating retroactively if the customs declaration, transport evidence, or foreign exchange receipt is missing, falsified, or not collected within the statutory period. The normal statute of limitations for a VAT assessment is 5 years, extended to 10 years for fraudulent evasion. Where zero-rating is overturned, NTS will assess the 10% VAT on the domestic supply, impose statutory additional tax under the Value-Added Tax Act for underpayment or failure to issue proper tax invoices, charge monthly late-payment interest, and may challenge the export if foreign exchange proceeds are not repatriated by the 180-day foreign exchange settlement deadline. If the false zero-rating is accompanied by intentional documentary fraud, the matter is referred under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, which exposes the responsible officers to criminal fines and imprisonment, and the refund claim is clawed back with a 40% unjustifiable refund penalty.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), exercising delegated authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) operated in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Korean won is fully convertible on current account transactions, including routine trade settlement and service payments, subject to reporting and supporting documentation under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital account transactions are restricted and require prior approval or report to the Bank of Korea via an authorised foreign exchange bank, particularly for foreign direct investment, overseas borrowing, and loans between related parties. Dividend and profit remittances for foreign investors are generally free once audited retained earnings and corporate tax liabilities are verified, but banks require a tax payment certificate, audited financial statements, and BOK FDI registration proof. For an LLC manufacturing freeze-dried pet raw meat, export proceeds from overseas distributors must be collected through a Korean authorised foreign exchange bank and reported to the FEIS; there is no current statutory surrender ratio forcing conversion into KRW, meaning exporters may hold eligible foreign currency in a designated account, but domestic operating expenses are normally paid in KRW so treasury policy should plan for conversion drag. Temporary liquidity constraints can arise if export invoices are matched late or forward invoices do not have confirmed underlying trade documentation, because banks treat unsubstantiated currency conversions as speculative and may reject or delay them. Overall, the regime is liberal on operational trade flows but compliance-intensive for capital injections and shareholder loans, demanding a pre-approved FX compliance framework before funding.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds for goods must be collected within 15 months of the export declaration date through an authorised foreign exchange bank in Korea, unless a valid extension is granted by the Ministry of Economy and Finance. There is no mandatory percentage surrender to KRW under current regulations; exporters may retain eligible foreign exchange receipts in a designated foreign currency account. The receipt must be reported to the BOK Foreign Exchange Information System (FEIS) with the export declaration number, invoice details, and underlying trade contract, and the exporting entity must provide proof of actual receipt before using the funds for settlement, transfers, or dividend remittance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore digital EMIs are legally barred from providing Korean domestic currency accounts or corporate banking services to a domestic LLC unless they hold a Korean electronic financial business license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and public notification to the Financial Supervisory Service. No major licensed cross-border EMI currently offers a viable standalone treasury solution for a manufacturing entity with inbound FDI and outbound trade flows. The entity may use an international payment platform merely as a client-facing collection channel if settlement is ultimately channelled through an authorised Korean foreign exchange bank, but doing so creates reconciliation, VAT, and AML shadow-account risks. Therefore, the treasury blueprint should rely on licensed Tier-1 domestic banks for all primary clearing, with EMI routes rejected as a substitute.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For first-time corporate onboarding of a new Korean LLC with foreign shareholders, the statutory director(s), the registered account signatories, and, where requested, the ultimate beneficial owners must attend an in-branch interview in South Korea. Remote consular proxy account opening is not accepted by major commercial banks for operational corporate accounts, because the Financial Action Task Force guidance and Korean financial institution KYC standards require direct verification of identity and business purpose. If travel is impossible, the bank may accept a consular legalised power of attorney and apostilled certificates, but only if a resident company officer is physically present at the bank with the corporate seal, original articles, and shareholder resolutions; this route is consistently subject to additional AML interviews and delayed approval.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification gap caused by a Korean LLC nominee ownership layer or franchised manufacturing arrangement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate registry issuances, shareholder register, UBO declaration form, notarised ownership chain, tax identification numbers and passports of all natural person owners, plus a written explanation and supporting contracts for any nominee arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector red flag: raw meat inputs for freeze-dried pet treats create high-risk trade-based money laundering and cross-border disease-control exposures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) veterinary inspection certificates, Korean quarantine certificates, import health certificates from source countries, proof of physical premises and equipment, purchase contracts with licensed slaughterhouses, and bank-verified trade invoices matching the actual capacity of the freeze-drying line.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for initial capital injection and shareholder loans from foreign investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statement history of the source account, audited financial statements or tax records of the investor, signed capital contribution resolution, FIPA report to BOK, stamp and tax clearance, and legalised translation of all funding agreements; insist on direct bank-to-bank wire with full remitter name and TED/OBI fields.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactional velocity mismatch: expected high-frequency SWIFT TT receipts from e-commerce pet food platforms may violate account-purpose and transaction-monitoring profiles
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved business model and platform agreements listing expected settlement curves, invoice-level trade documentation, customer contract library, FEIS report filings, and quarterly transaction flow projections; establish separate collection and disbursement accounts if needed.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound funding must be routed from the investor's own bank account via SWIFT to a designated KRW or foreign currency capital escrow account at an authorised Korean foreign exchange bank. The remittance purpose must be recorded as foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and reported to the BOK Foreign Exchange Information System within the statutory reporting deadline, which in practice is satisfied before the bank issues the foreign currency receipt certificate and certificate of capital paid-in based on registered share issuance. If the capital is contributed in kind or as a convertible loan, amendments and tax filings must be completed first. For all capital contributions, every supporting document, including the shareholders meeting resolution, the investment contract, the final invoice and bank receipt, must be cross-referenced and preserved for the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the National Tax Service, and the banking compliance committee.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For supplier and raw meat import settlements, use SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for utility and low-value payments; for bulk raw meat procurement use Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections (D/P and D/A) to reduce trade-based financing risk. Payments must be submitted with invoice, packing list, bill of lading, quarantine certificate, and tax invoice; outbound amounts must match the approved FEIS purpose code. For freeze-dried pet raw meat exported to overseas distributors, received foreign currency must be reconciled to each export declaration before conversion and before any dividend remittance; dividends can be converted only after external audit completion if there is no accumulated deficit, via the authorised foreign exchange bank's dividend remittance review with corporate tax withholding proof.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Licensed KRW/USD and KRW/EUR vanilla FX forwards with authorised foreign exchange banks, supported by real export or import exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with an overseas banking arm of a domestic licensed bank, executed only where the underlying trade exposure is verified and the instrument is hedge-only
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for matured foreign investor loans or capital-contribution hedges, capped at outstanding principal and documented by the underlying capital agreement
Bank-issued FX options limited to hedging genuine commercial exposures, prohibited when structured as leveraged or speculative products

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Return including Local Income Tax Surtax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via Hometax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the following year for a December 31 fiscal year end; general rule is within 3 months after the fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers a 20% of unpaid tax penalty, raised to 40% for fraudulent or aggravated false returns; a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.0225% of unpaid tax accrues from the day after the due date, generally capped at 9%. The NTS may make a discretionary tax assessment, seize assets, and cancel the business registration for prolonged delinquency; Korean law does not maintain an administrative strike-off for private limited companies, but forced collection can economically dissolve the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Preliminary Return for January to March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via Hometax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 25 following the first calendar quarter.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers VAT additional tax of 10% of unpaid VAT, or 20% for repeat offenses, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.0225% up to 9%. No administrative strike-off; enforcement is through tax assessment and asset attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers VAT additional tax of 10% of unpaid VAT, or 20% for repeat offenses, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.0225% up to 9%. No administrative strike-off; enforcement is through tax assessment and asset attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via Hometax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers VAT additional tax of 10% of unpaid VAT, or 20% for repeat offenses, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.0225% up to 9%. No administrative strike-off; enforcement is through tax assessment and asset attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via Hometax

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers VAT additional tax of 10% of unpaid VAT, or 20% for repeat offenses, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.0225% up to 9%. No administrative strike-off; enforcement is through tax assessment and asset attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Tax Interim Prepayment for the First Half-Year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of South Korea (NTS) via Hometax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By August 31 for a calendar-year entity, within 2 months after the interim closing date of June 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underpayment or non-filing produces an additional tax of 10% of the shortfall plus the daily late-payment surcharge of 0.0225% of unpaid tax, generally capped at 9%; prolonged non-compliance triggers forced collection and tax seizure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) / Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before June 30 following each fiscal year for foreign-invested enterprises; the calendar window applies to the preceding fiscal year's investment and operational status.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing a false report can result in administrative fines generally up to KRW 10,000,000, or higher for aggravated cases, and possible cancellation of the foreign-invested enterprise registration with KOTRA; no corporate strike-off is triggered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Member Meeting and Financial Statement Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate registry evidence; proof of approval is retained with corporate records and relied upon for the NTS corporate tax filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year end, i.e., by March 31 for a December 31 calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No administrative strike-off; failure to convene the annual member meeting or approve financial statements may subject directors to civil liability, invalidate reliance on financial statements for tax loss carry-forward claims, and permit a member to petition the Korean court for judicial supervision or dissolution in extreme deadlock cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Joint-Stock Companies and its Enforcement Decree, a Yuhan Hoesa must appoint an independent certified CPA auditor if, at fiscal year-end, total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9 million); or total assets equal or exceed KRW 7 billion and the company meets qualifying Enforcement Decree criteria such as 100 or more regular employees, high debt-to-equity ratio, or material annual turnover; or the company is designated as a large corporation by the Financial Services Commission. Listed companies and certain public-interest entities are audited regardless of size. Pet food manufacturing companies below these thresholds are not statutory-audit subjects, but must prepare accurate accrual-basis financial statements for corporate tax filing and may require a certified tax accountant's review for VAT and income tax purposes.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for public-interest corporations and mandatory-audit large companies; K-GAAP General Corporate Accounting Standards for non-public companies; Korean SME Accounting Standards for eligible small and medium enterprises. All statutory accounting must follow the Commercial Act's financial statement presentation requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Korean law does not impose a simple annual UBO form in the same manner as European registries. Under the Act on Management of Beneficial Ownership Information in Commercial Registration, a Yuhan Hoesa must maintain beneficial-owner records and report any transfer of membership interests or change in ultimate beneficial ownership to the Commercial Registry Court within 30 days. The court runs a periodic re-verification cycle, generally triennial, for existing companies. Separately, a foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa must confirm the foreign beneficial-owner percentage and shareholding structure in the Annual Foreign Investment Report filed with KOTRA by June 30 following each fiscal year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Managing Officers and Auditors
Register of Statutory Liens or Charges over Membership Interests

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 2,500 per year for registered address, local corporate secretarial services, and commercial registry maintenance in South Korea, depending on city and service scope.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 per year for a small to mid-sized freeze-dried pet food manufacturing Yuhan Hoesa requiring a certified CPA audit; a certified tax accountant review-only fee is typically USD 2,500 - USD 6,000.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surcharge on the national CIT, producing a combined 29.7% top marginal rate
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive 9%-27% schedule; SME rate deductions; R&D tax credits; foreign-investment tax reductions and cash grants in Free Economic Zones; limited preferential none for freeze-dried pet food manufacturing itself; carryforward loss offset capped at 5 filing years in this compliance mapping

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Domestic Corporation and Local Income Tax Return, filed electronically through the Korean National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; one-month extension may be available when a certified tax accountant prepares the return and audited financial statements are attached

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, legal entity name, representative director, fiscal year-end, accounting method, and non-resident investor identification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean LLC business registration number exactly; disclose every non-resident shareholder and its residence jurisdiction because omitted nominees create a fatal red flag and trigger withholding and reporting failures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book income or loss, statutory add-backs, non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, prior-year loss offset, and transfer-pricing adjustments to arrive at taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Substantiate all freeze-dried pet raw material costs and platform sales under Corporate Tax Act Article 19; reverse unsupported expenses; include cross-border related-party adjustments at arm's length before applying the 5-year loss carryover ceiling.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Progressive tax rate computation and calculation of national corporate income tax plus the 10% local income tax surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate taxable income at the entity level; non-resident shareholder dividend exposure is reported separately and should not be netted against the Korean entity's corporate income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credit, withholding tax credit, special deductions, and tax-exemption computations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach credible foreign tax credit evidence; DTA relief for outbound payments is not claimed inside this box and must be supported by the beneficial owner's TRC and substance documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of dividends, interest, and royalties paid or credited to non-residents during the tax year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Strictly withhold 20% national WHT plus 2% local income tax surcharge unless a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership statement are collected before payment; treaty relief rates require a Korean NTS treaty exemption/reduction application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party international transaction disclosure and contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all foreign related-party transactions in KRW; prepare and submit Local File and Master File when annual related-party cross-border transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; specify the selected arm's-length method and economic substance basis.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3, late filing adds a 20% penalty on unpaid tax; negligent underreporting 10%; intentional underreporting 40%; late payment surcharge accrues at 0.03% per day; separate fines up to KRW 50 million apply for failure to file international transaction statements and TP documentation, plus criminal liability under Corporate Tax Act Article 109.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national dividend withholding tax plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the withheld amount, combined 22%, on dividends paid to non-residents
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The Korean withholding agent must collect the non-resident shareholder's current Tax Residency Certificate issued by the residence-country tax authority, a signed beneficial ownership declaration, and the NTS application for treaty rate reduction/exemption before payment; if the recipient lacks real business substance or is a conduit, DTA benefits are denied and the 22% combined WHT is reassessed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 20% national WHT on royalties and interest plus 2% local income tax, totaling 22%; Korea-US DTA commonly reduces interest and royalty WHT to 10%, while other Korean DTAs generally provide 10%-15% rates subject to limitation-on-benefits conditions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 5,000,000,000 annual value of intercompany transactions with foreign related parties triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation and submission through the international transaction statement
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea has no standalone offshore-style ESR regime, but the NTS applies substance-over-form, OECD BEPS principal purpose tests, beneficial ownership standards, CFC rules, and anti-conduit doctrines to deny treaty benefits where the Korean freeze-dried pet food manufacturing entity lacks Core Income-Generating Activities such as real operational employees, production premises, and decision-making autonomy.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion by Underreporting and False Bookkeeping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omission of platform payment-rail sales and fabrication of freeze-dried pet raw meat production costs in the Korean LLC's corporate income tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 109 of the Corporate Tax Act: imprisonment for up to 3 years and fines up to 3 times the evaded tax; Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-3 imposes an additional 40% unfair underreporting penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil piercing under Commercial Act Articles 321 and 401; the NTS may seize personal assets, blacklist the director as a delinquent taxpayer, impose an overseas travel ban, and pursue criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Disclosure and Non-Arm's-Length Cross-Border Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling pet food to a foreign affiliated company below cost or paying excessive royalties/intercompany interest without filing the international transaction statement and contemporaneous TP documentation above the KRW 5 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Framework Act on International Tax Coordination Article 4 authorizes arm's-length re-determination; failure to maintain and submit TP files triggers separate monetary fines, plus negligent or intentional underreporting penalties of 10% to 40% of the assessed additional tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certify false TP disclosures are jointly liable for the reassessed CIT, surcharges and penalties; the NTS may place directors on the travel-ban blacklist and bring criminal fraud charges if the adjustment is part of a deliberate evasion scheme.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Treaty Abuse in Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing Korean LLC dividends, interest, or royalties through a letterbox holding company in a treaty jurisdiction with no employees, premises, or commercial purpose solely to reduce Korean WHT on repatriated profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Restriction of Special Taxation Act Article 73 allows denial of treaty benefits; reassessment is made at the statutory 20% national WHT plus 2% local surtax; withholding agents face liability under Corporate Tax Act Article 12 and criminal penalties under Article 109.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and effective owners face veil-piercing civil liability for unpaid withholding taxes, personal asset restitution, tax-delinquent blacklisting with overseas travel bans, and imprisonment of up to 3 years for fraudulent structuring.
